question: The five functions of management in their correct order are:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. planning, organising, staffing, directing and controlling

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Management begins with planning, is followed by organising the work, staffing the posts, directing the people and finally controlling through evaluation

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — organising, planning, directing, staffing and controlling: Organising cannot precede planning

C — staffing, directing, planning, controlling and organising: Staffing follows organising and not planning

D — controlling, planning, staffing, organising and directing: Controlling is the last and not the first step

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nursing officer plans the month's activity before she posts the staff, because a roster drawn before the plan is a roster that is redrawn within the week

question: A 30 bed surgical ward has eight patients who are fully dependent, twelve who need help with most activities and ten who are self caring. The nursing officer should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. calculate the nursing hours from the dependency categories and post the staff accordingly

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The nursing hours required are worked out from the dependency of the patients, and the staffing is then matched to that figure

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — allot the same number of nurses to each patient: Equal allotment gives the dependent patient the same time as the self caring one

C — keep only two nurses on the night duty in every case: A fixed night posting takes no account of the number of dependent patients that night

D — leave the posting to the staff's own convenience: Staff convenience is considered after the safety of the patients and not before it

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nursing officer recalculates the dependency every shift, because the patient who becomes dependent at midnight is the one the fixed posting leaves uncovered
option_1: allot the same number of nurses to each patient
option_2: calculate the nursing hours from the dependency categories and post the staff accordingly
option_3: keep only two nurses on the night duty in every case
option_4: leave the posting to the staff's own convenience

question: While preparing the monthly duty roster of a ward the nursing officer should FIRST ensure that:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. the ward is covered by nurses of the required grade in every shift

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Safe coverage of every shift by a nurse of the required grade is the first requirement of a roster, and the preferences of the staff are adjusted around it

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — the preferences of the senior most nurse are met: Seniority does not decide the pattern of the roster

C — every nurse gets the same number of night duties: An even share of night duty is desirable and comes after the requirement of coverage

D — no nurse is posted with a colleague she dislikes: Personal likes are not a principle of rostering

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nursing officer posts the roster a week in advance and shows it to the staff, because a roster that appears on the morning it takes effect is a roster that is argued with at the bedside
option_1: the ward is covered by nurses of the required grade in every shift
option_2: the preferences of the senior most nurse are met
option_3: every nurse gets the same number of night duties
option_4: no nurse is posted with a colleague she dislikes

question: The nursing officer finds that the ward has spent 90 per cent of its annual budget in the first six months. The most appropriate action is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. analyse the spending against the plan, cut the avoidable items and place the essential needs before the administration

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Overspending is corrected by studying what was bought against the plan, cutting what can be deferred and putting the unavoidable requirements before the administration with reasons

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — stop buying all consumables until the year ends: Stopping every purchase endangers patient care

B — ask the staff to bring some consumables from home: Asking the staff to supply consumables is improper and unsafe

C — spend the remaining 10 per cent as quickly as possible: Hurrying the rest of the spending adds to the deficit

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nursing officer reviews the expenditure every month and not at the half year, because a trend that is watched monthly is a trend that can still be turned
option_1: stop buying all consumables until the year ends
option_2: ask the staff to bring some consumables from home
option_3: spend the remaining 10 per cent as quickly as possible
option_4: analyse the spending against the plan, cut the avoidable items and place the essential needs before the administration

question: A ward store shows that a high value dressing material has been issued in large quantities for three months without a matching use in the ward. The nursing officer should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. verify the indent, the stock on the shelf and the ward register and establish the consumption pattern

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A mismatch between issue and use is looked into by matching the indent, the physical stock and the register, and the pattern is then established before any conclusion

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — stop issuing the material to the ward: Withholding a material that patients need punishes the patients

B — ignore it, since the material was prescribed by the doctors: Ignoring the difference allows a loss to continue unchecked

C — report the store keeper to the police at once: An accusation made before the facts are known is unjust and cannot be withdrawn

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nursing officer does a surprise physical check of the emergency tray every month, because a stock that is only counted on paper is a stock that fails on the night it is needed
option_1: stop issuing the material to the ward
option_2: ignore it, since the material was prescribed by the doctors
option_3: report the store keeper to the police at once
option_4: verify the indent, the stock on the shelf and the ward register and establish the consumption pattern

question: The main purpose of accreditation of a hospital by the National Accreditation Board for Hospitals is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. ensure that defined standards of patient care and safety are met and continuously improved

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Accreditation is an external review against published standards of care, safety and management, and its purpose is improvement in what the patient receives

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — attract foreign patients: Patients from any country may benefit, but that is a consequence and not the purpose

C — reduce the number of nurses employed: Staffing is determined by the workload and the standards of care

D — increase the charges of the hospital: The charges of a hospital follow its cost structure and not its accreditation

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse keeps the accreditation manual in the ward and not in the office, because the standard that is never read is the standard that is never followed
option_2: ensure that defined standards of patient care and safety are met and continuously improved

question: A ward report that is handed over at the change of shift should contain:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. a concise account of the condition, the treatment and the special observations of each patient

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A handover report carries the facts the next shift needs to continue the care safely

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the list of the patients who are likely to complain: Anticipating complaints is not clinical information

C — the nurse's opinion of the patients and the staff: Opinions of the staff have no place in a clinical report

D — the private matters discussed by the patients: Private matters of patients are confidential

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reads the report back to the oncoming nurse at the bedside of the sickest patient, because a report that is only spoken at the table loses the very patients it was meant to protect
option_1: the list of the patients who are likely to complain
option_2: a concise account of the condition, the treatment and the special observations of each patient
option_3: the nurse's opinion of the patients and the staff
option_4: the private matters discussed by the patients

question: A newly posted staff nurse is asked to take charge of the ward for the night. The nursing officer should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. orient her to the ward, the equipment and the reporting line and keep a senior nurse available for consultation

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A nurse newly given charge is oriented to the ward and the equipment and is told clearly whom to call, with a senior available for support

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — postpone her night duty until she has five years of service: Service of five years is not a requirement of the post

B — leave her entirely on her own so that she learns quickly: Responsibility given without support is the setting in which errors happen

C — give her the keys and ask her to manage as best she can: Handing over the keys is not supervision

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nursing officer makes one round of the ward with the new charge nurse before midnight, because a nurse who has been shown the dark corners once is a nurse who will find them again
option_1: postpone her night duty until she has five years of service
option_2: leave her entirely on her own so that she learns quickly
option_3: give her the keys and ask her to manage as best she can
option_4: orient her to the ward, the equipment and the reporting line and keep a senior nurse available for consultation

question: A ward has experienced nurses who work well together and need little direction. The leadership style that suits this group best is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. democratic with delegated responsibility

🧠 Clinical Rationale: An experienced and motivated team works best in a participative setting in which responsibility is delegated and the leader remains available

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — laissez faire with no supervision at all: Complete freedom without any supervision removes the accountability the leader still holds

B — bureaucratic with a rule for every act: Rigid rule following delays decisions that the group could take at once

D — autocratic: Autocratic control frustrates a group that does not need to be driven

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nursing officer matches the style to the maturity of the group and not to her own comfort, because a style that suits one ward destroys the initiative of another
option_1: laissez faire with no supervision at all
option_2: bureaucratic with a rule for every act

question: The doctors and the nurses of a unit disagree repeatedly over the timing of the morning rounds. The nursing officer's most constructive step is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. bring both sides together, find the common interest of the patients and agree on a workable timing

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A recurring difference between two groups is settled by bringing them together around the interest they share and agreeing on a workable arrangement

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — instruct the nurses to comply without discussion: An instruction without discussion suppresses the problem and not the cause

C — report the doctors to the medical superintendent: A complaint made before an attempt at settlement hardens the two sides

D — leave the matter to resolve itself: Standing aside allows the friction to affect the care

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nursing officer settles the issue on the basis of what the patients need and not of who was right, because a solution built on victory for one side is reopened within a fortnight
option_1: bring both sides together, find the common interest of the patients and agree on a workable timing
option_2: instruct the nurses to comply without discussion
option_3: report the doctors to the medical superintendent

question: A staff nurse has been irregular in coming to duty for a month. The correct sequence of action is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. speak to her privately, find the reason, record the discussion and take formal action only if it continues

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A first lapse is dealt with by a private enquiry into the cause, a record of the discussion and a warning that further lapse will bring formal action

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — report her to the police: Absence from duty is an administrative matter and not a police matter

C — transfer her to another ward at once: Transferring the nurse takes the problem to another ward and leaves it unsolved

D — warn her in writing first and speak to her afterwards: A written warning before any enquiry is both unjust and premature

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nursing officer puts the talk on record the same day with the date and the outcome, because a pattern that is never written down cannot be corrected and cannot be defended either
option_1: speak to her privately, find the reason, record the discussion and take formal action only if it continues
option_3: transfer her to another ward at once
option_4: warn her in writing first and speak to her afterwards

question: Nursing audit is best described as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. a systematic review of the records of care against an accepted standard with a view to improving it

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Nursing audit compares what was actually recorded and done with an accepted standard and then acts on the difference found

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a list of the nurses who have completed a year of service: A list of staff is a personnel document and audits nothing

B — an inspection of the nurse's uniform and appearance: Inspection of appearance is a part of discipline and not of audit

D — the count of the patients treated in a month: A count of patients is a statistical fact and not a review of care

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nursing officer shares the audit findings with the staff who gave the care, because an audit whose findings remain with the officer changes nothing in the ward
option_1: a list of the nurses who have completed a year of service
option_2: an inspection of the nurse's uniform and appearance
option_3: a systematic review of the records of care against an accepted standard with a view to improving it
option_4: the count of the patients treated in a month

question: After a serious medication error the person best placed to write the incident report is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. the nurse who made the error

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The person who was present at the event writes the factual account, since she alone knows exactly what happened and when

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the nurse in charge, since she was not involved: A second hand report loses the detail that makes the report useful

B — the doctor who corrected the error: The doctor records his treatment, and the incident report is the nurse's document

C — the patient's relative: A relative cannot record facts she did not observe

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nursing officer receives the report without any question of blame in the first hour, because a staff who expect punishment report the twelfth error and not the first
option_1: the nurse in charge, since she was not involved

question: The statement of the problem in a research study should be:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. clear, specific and researchable within the available time and resources

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A problem statement is useful only when it is clear, focused and capable of being studied with the means at hand

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — written after the data have been collected: The problem is stated before the data are collected

B — broad enough to cover every aspect of nursing: A statement that is too broad cannot be answered by any single study

C — the same as the conclusion of the study: A conclusion is drawn from the findings and is not the statement of the problem

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse begins with a question arising from her own practice, because a study that grows out of a ward problem is the one whose answer is used in that ward
option_1: written after the data have been collected
option_2: broad enough to cover every aspect of nursing
option_3: the same as the conclusion of the study
option_4: clear, specific and researchable within the available time and resources

question: In simple random sampling:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. every member of the population has an equal chance of being selected

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Simple random sampling gives each member of the defined population an equal and independent chance of selection through a lottery, a table of random numbers or a computer

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — every fifth member after a random start is chosen: Every fifth member after a random start is systematic sampling

B — the population is first divided into strata: Dividing the population into groups is stratified sampling

C — the members are chosen by the investigator's judgement: Selection by judgement is purposive sampling

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse states the population and the method of selection in the report, because a sample whose selection cannot be described can never be trusted however large it is
option_1: every fifth member after a random start is chosen
option_2: the population is first divided into strata
option_3: the members are chosen by the investigator's judgement
option_4: every member of the population has an equal chance of being selected

question: A nurse wants to study the practice of hand hygiene in a 600 bed hospital and selects 30 nurses from each of the medical, surgical, obstetric and paediatric units. The method used is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. stratified random sampling

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The population is divided into groups of a known character and a sample is drawn from each group, which is stratified sampling and ensures that every type of unit is represented

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — purposive sampling: Purposive sampling chooses on judgement and not to represent the strata

C — snowball sampling: In snowball sampling one subject refers the next

D — simple random sampling: Simple random sampling would not guarantee a share for each unit

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reports the response of each stratum separately, because a good practice in the obstetric unit and a poor one in the medical unit cancel out in a single combined figure

question: The diagram best suited to compare the number of patients admitted in five different hospitals in one year is a:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. simple bar diagram

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A simple bar diagram compares distinct groups in one category and shows the differences between whole numbers at a glance

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — histogram: A histogram is used for continuous grouped data and not for named institutions

C — pie diagram: A pie diagram shows the parts of a single whole and not five separate totals

D — frequency polygon: A frequency polygon describes one distribution as a line and is used for comparison of distributions, not of totals

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse keeps all the bars the same width and the scale starting at zero, because a bar diagram that is drawn to flatter a favourite hospital is a diagram that misleads the reader

question: The lengths of stay in days of six patients are 4, 5, 5, 6, 7 and 21. The measure that best represents the typical length of stay is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. median

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The patient who stayed twenty one days pulls the mean upwards, so the median of five and a half days describes the usual stay more honestly

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — range: The range is a measure of spread and says nothing about the typical value

B — mean: The mean works out to about eight days, which no patient except one came near

D — mode: The mode does describe one common value but ignores the rest of the data

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reports the median length of stay in a ward report, because a single long stay patient can make an efficient ward look slow on the strength of the average alone

question: In a normal distribution curve, the mean, the median and the mode:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. all fall at the same central point and the curve is symmetrical about it

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A normal distribution is symmetrical and bell shaped, so the mean, the median and the mode coincide at its centre and about sixty eight per cent of the readings lie within one standard deviation on either side

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — cannot be located on the curve: All three measures can be located from the curve

C — fall at three widely separated points: Separated points describe a skewed distribution

D — fall at the two ends of the curve: The ends are the tails of the curve and hold the extreme values

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse judges whether a set of readings is roughly normal before quoting a mean and a standard deviation, because those two figures describe a symmetrical set and mislead when the readings are gathered at one end
option_2: all fall at the same central point and the curve is symmetrical about it
option_4: fall at the two ends of the curve

question: In a hospital with 500 deliveries in a year there were 15 maternal deaths. The maternal mortality ratio is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 30 per 1000 live births

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The maternal mortality ratio is the number of maternal deaths in a year divided by the number of live births in the same year and multiplied by a thousand, so fifteen divided by five hundred gives thirty

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 3 per 1000 live births: Three per thousand would need only one and a half deaths

C — 15 per 1000 live births: Fifteen per thousand leaves out the multiplication

D — 150 per 1000 live births: One hundred and fifty per thousand would need seventy five deaths

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse uses live births and not the total population as the denominator for maternal deaths, because the total population would drown the risk of the woman who actually gives birth

question: In an experimental research design the investigator:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. controls and manipulates the independent variable to study its effect

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The experiment is the design in which the investigator introduces or controls the treatment and then measures its effect

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — only observes and describes what happens: Mere observation describes a survey

C — studies a single patient in detail: The study of a single patient in depth is a case study

D — looks backwards at records already written: Looking back at old records describes a retrospective study

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse checks that the two groups were comparable before the treatment began, because an effect seen in groups that differed from the start proves nothing about the treatment
option_2: controls and manipulates the independent variable to study its effect

question: In a case control study the investigator:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. starts with the people who have the disease and looks back for the exposure that may have caused it

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The case control design begins with the outcome already present and compares the past exposure of the cases with that of the controls

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — gives the treatment and measures the outcome: Giving a treatment and measuring the effect describes a trial

C — studies the whole population at one point in time: Studying a population at one point of time describes a cross sectional study

D — follows a group forward in time to see who develops the disease: Following a group forward describes a cohort study

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse selects controls from the same population that produced the cases, because a control group drawn from a different kind of people produces a difference that belongs to the people and not to the exposure
option_1: starts with the people who have the disease and looks back for the exposure that may have caused it
option_2: gives the treatment and measures the outcome
option_3: studies the whole population at one point in time
option_4: follows a group forward in time to see who develops the disease

question: Before a nurse enrols patients in a research study she must:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. obtain the approval of the institutional ethics committee and the informed consent of the patients

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A study on human beings needs the clearance of the ethics committee, and each participant must give a free and informed consent after being told the purpose, the risks and the right to withdraw

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — keep the purpose of the study secret from the patients: Concealing the purpose removes the very basis of a valid consent

C — promise the patients that the new treatment will cure them: A promise of cure is untrue and destroys the consent

D — begin with the patients who are least likely to object: Choosing those who will not object is neither consent nor fair selection

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse tells the patient in writing that he may withdraw at any time without any effect on his treatment, because the freedom to leave is what makes a consent voluntary
option_1: keep the purpose of the study secret from the patients
option_2: obtain the approval of the institutional ethics committee and the informed consent of the patients
option_3: promise the patients that the new treatment will cure them
option_4: begin with the patients who are least likely to object

question: A result that is described as significant at the 5 per cent level means that:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. a difference as large as the one found would occur by chance less than five times in a hundred

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The five per cent level is the risk the investigator accepts of calling a difference real when it is in fact due to chance, so such a difference arises by chance less than five times in a hundred

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the treatment works in ninety five per cent of the patients: A significant result is not a statement about the success rate of the treatment

B — the study has five per cent of the planned sample: It has nothing to do with the size of the sample

C — the result is five per cent wrong: The value states the risk of a false positive finding and not a general error of five per cent

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reads the confidence interval along with the level of significance, because a result may be statistically significant and still be too small to matter to a patient
option_1: the treatment works in ninety five per cent of the patients
option_2: the study has five per cent of the planned sample
option_3: the result is five per cent wrong
option_4: a difference as large as the one found would occur by chance less than five times in a hundred

question: The size of the sample required for a study is decided mainly by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. the size of the difference expected, the variability of the measurement and the level of confidence desired

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A sample must be large enough to show the smallest difference that matters, and the calculation depends on the expected difference, the variability of the readings and the confidence and power that are wanted

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the number of patients available in the ward on the day of the visit: Convenience of the day's attendance is not a statistical basis

B — the wish of the investigator: Personal wish cannot replace a calculation

D — the number of pages allowed for the report: The length of the report is settled after the study is designed

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse fixes the sample size before the data collection begins, because a sample enlarged after the results have looked disappointing is a sample whose conclusion can no longer be believed
option_1: the number of patients available in the ward on the day of the visit
option_3: the size of the difference expected, the variability of the measurement and the level of confidence desired
option_4: the number of pages allowed for the report

question: In a study of 200 patients the length of stay and the number of bed sores show a correlation coefficient of plus 0.82. The nurse should conclude that:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. there is a strong positive relationship between the two, though the study does not prove that one causes the other

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A coefficient near plus one indicates a strong positive relationship, but a correlation by itself does not establish the direction of cause

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the two variables are unrelated: A coefficient of plus 0.82 is far from zero and the two are clearly related

B — a longer stay causes bed sores: The coefficient cannot show which variable came first

D — bed sores shorten the stay: The sign of the coefficient is positive, so the two move in the same direction

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reads a correlation as a signal to study further and not as a conclusion, because the pressure sore and the long stay arise together from the same poor mobility
option_3: there is a strong positive relationship between the two, though the study does not prove that one causes the other

question: The first and foremost responsibility of the nurse according to the code of ethics is towards:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. the patient

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The code places the care of the patient and the respect for his rights and dignity above every other duty

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the professional council: The Council governs the profession and comes after the patient in the order of duty

C — the doctor: Co-operation with the doctor is essential but is not placed above the patient

D — the employer: The duties to the employer follow the duty to the patient

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse remembers that an instruction from anyone does not release her from her own duty to the patient, because the responsibility to the patient is personal and cannot be transferred

question: A 60 year old woman who is fully conscious is to undergo a biopsy and her son signs the consent form for her. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. ask the patient herself to read and sign the consent, since she is conscious and competent

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A conscious and competent adult gives consent for herself, and a relative cannot give it on her behalf however close the relationship

🔍 Key Clues: 60 year old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — accept the son's consent, as he is the closest relative: A relative's signature is valid only when the patient is unable to give consent

B — ask both the son and the patient to sign: A signature taken from a competent patient and a relative together only confuses the record

D — proceed without any consent, as the test is minor: No procedure is done without consent

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse satisfies herself that the patient has understood the nature and the risk of the procedure, because a signature taken without understanding is only ink on a page
option_1: accept the son's consent, as he is the closest relative
option_2: ask both the son and the patient to sign
option_3: ask the patient herself to read and sign the consent, since she is conscious and competent
option_4: proceed without any consent, as the test is minor

question: A 45 year old patient slips on a wet floor beside his bed and fractures his hip, and the floor had just been mopped without any warning sign. The likely finding is that:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. the hospital failed in its duty of care to keep the premises safe

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The hospital owes a duty to keep the patient safe from a known hazard, and mopping without a warning sign is a breach of that duty that has ended in harm

🔍 Key Clues: 45 year old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — the patient was careless and the hospital has no duty: A patient in a ward is entitled to assume that the floor is safe

C — the cleaning staff alone are personally liable: The employer carries the liability for the acts of the staff in the course of their work

D — the fracture was unrelated to the floor: A causal link between the wet floor and the fall is clear

question: A nurse gives an injection into the wrong buttock site and the patient develops a sciatic nerve palsy. In law:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. the nurse is answerable for her own act and the hospital is answerable vicariously for the act done in the course of duty

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The nurse carries personal professional liability and the employer carries vicarious liability for the act done by an employee in the course of the employment

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — no one is answerable, since the patient's anatomy was unusual: The accepted site of an intramuscular injection is taught precisely so that this injury is avoided

B — only the hospital is answerable: The nurse is not protected from personal liability by the hospital's liability

D — only the nurse is answerable: The employer's liability does not remove the nurse's own

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

question: A nursing student discusses the diagnosis of a patient with her friends outside the hospital. Her conduct is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. a breach of confidentiality and of the code of professional conduct

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The duty of confidentiality follows the patient and not the place, and information about a patient is disclosed only to those who need it for his care

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — acceptable, since the discussion was outside the hospital: The place of the conversation does not change the duty

C — acceptable if the friends are also students of nursing: Fellow students who are not caring for that patient have no claim on the information

D — acceptable, since the patient was not named: A patient is easily recognised from the details even when the name is not spoken

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

option_4: acceptable, since the patient was not named

question: The best protection for a nurse facing an allegation of negligence is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. an accurate, complete and contemporaneous record of the care she gave

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The clinical record made at the time is the evidence that shows what was observed, what was done and when, and it is the nurse's strongest protection

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — her length of service in the hospital: Length of service establishes experience and not the facts of the day

B — a written statement prepared by her lawyer: A statement prepared later has to be supported by whatever was recorded at the time

C — the support of her colleagues: The support of colleagues is valuable but is not evidence of the care given

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

option_4: an accurate, complete and contemporaneous record of the care she gave

question: An alert and fully informed adult patient refuses a blood transfusion that the doctor considers necessary to save his life. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. respect the refusal, record it clearly and inform the doctor

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A competent adult may refuse any treatment, even one that is needed to save his life, and the refusal is recorded with the time and the person informed

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — ask the relatives to sign their consent instead: The relatives have no authority to override a competent patient

B — give the transfusion in any case, since life is at stake: A transfusion given against a valid refusal is a trespass on the person

C — tell the patient that he will be discharged if he refuses: Discharge is not a punishment for the exercise of a right

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

question: A 6 year old child with a flat nasal bridge, upward slanting eyes and a karyotype report of 47 chromosomes has the extra chromosome at pair:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 21

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The features described are those of Down syndrome, in which an extra copy of chromosome 21 gives a total of forty seven chromosomes

🔍 Key Clues: 6 year old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 18: Trisomy 18 gives a small jaw, clenched fists and a poor outlook

B — 13: Trisomy 13 gives defects of the face and the brain with a very short survival

C — 23: Pair 23 is the sex chromosome pair and an extra copy there gives a different syndrome

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse explains the karyotype report to the parents in plain words at the time it arrives, because a report handed over without an explanation in the same visit is a report that the family takes home unanswered

question: In a monohybrid cross between two heterozygous parents the expected ratio of the offspring is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 3 to 1

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Two heterozygous parents produce three offspring showing the dominant trait for every one showing the recessive trait

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 9 to 3 to 3 to 1: Nine to three to three to one comes from a dihybrid cross

B — 1 to 1: A ratio of one to one comes from a cross between a heterozygous parent and a homozygous recessive one

D — 1 to 2 to 1: One to two to one is the ratio of the genotypes and not of the observable traits

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse tells the parents that the ratio describes the chances of each child and not the composition of their family, because a couple who have had three affected children hear the ratio as a promise that the next will be well

question: Colour blindness is an X linked recessive trait. This means that a colour blind man:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. passes the gene to all his daughters, who become carriers

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A man gives his single X chromosome to every daughter and his Y chromosome to every son, so all his daughters are carriers

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — passes the trait to half his daughters only: Every daughter and not half of them receives the gene

B — passes the trait to all his sons: A son receives his father's Y chromosome and not the affected X

C — cannot pass the gene to any of his children: The affected X chromosome is certainly passed on

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse advises the affected family to have the carrier status of the daughters tested before they marry, because the knowledge is useful only before the next generation begins
option_1: passes the trait to half his daughters only
option_2: passes the trait to all his sons
option_3: cannot pass the gene to any of his children
option_4: passes the gene to all his daughters, who become carriers

question: A woman with a normal karyotype but a history of three sons who died of a bleeding disorder is most probably:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. a carrier of an X linked recessive gene

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The loss of several sons while the mother herself is unaffected is the classic pattern of an X linked recessive gene carried by the mother

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — suffering from a chromosomal translocation of the autosomes: An autosomal translocation produces a wider and less sex linked pattern of loss

C — a carrier of an autosomal dominant gene: A dominant gene would show in the mother's own phenotype

D — affected by the disorder herself: An affected woman would show the disorder herself

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse draws the family tree with the sexes marked before any counselling is offered, because the pattern across the generations is what distinguishes one mode of inheritance from another
option_1: suffering from a chromosomal translocation of the autosomes
option_2: a carrier of an X linked recessive gene
option_3: a carrier of an autosomal dominant gene

question: An autosomal dominant disorder is one in which:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. a single abnormal gene on a non sex chromosome is enough to produce the disorder in every generation

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A dominant gene on an autosome produces the disorder even when its partner is normal, so the disorder appears in each generation

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the abnormal gene is carried on the X chromosome: A gene on the X chromosome gives a sex linked pattern

C — two abnormal genes are needed to produce the disorder: Two abnormal genes are needed for a recessive disorder

D — the disorder skips every second generation: Skipping generations is characteristic of a recessive trait

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse asks for the family history of both the parents before advising, because a dominant disorder that is seen in the parent's own family changes the risk figures the couple were given
option_1: the abnormal gene is carried on the X chromosome
option_2: a single abnormal gene on a non sex chromosome is enough to produce the disorder in every generation
option_3: two abnormal genes are needed to produce the disorder

question: A 28 year old woman whose first child died of thalassaemia asks the nurse whether her next child will be normal. The best response of the nurse is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. explain the one in four risk for each pregnancy, arrange testing of the husband and refer the couple for genetic counselling

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The risk for each pregnancy is set out, the father's carrier status is established by testing and the couple is referred for counselling so that they can decide with the facts in hand

🔍 Key Clues: 28 year old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — tell her that the risk cannot be known at all: The risk can be estimated once both the parents are tested

C — tell her not to have any more children: The decision about another pregnancy belongs to the couple

D — assure her that the next child will certainly be healthy: A promise of a healthy child is not hers to give and may be untrue

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse gives the figures and then leaves the decision to the couple without pressure, because a choice made freely is the one the family can live with afterwards

option_2: tell her that the risk cannot be known at all

option_4: assure her that the next child will certainly be healthy

question: A teratogen is best defined as an agent that:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. causes a structural or functional defect in the developing fetus

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A teratogen is any agent, such as a drug, an infection, alcohol or radiation, that disturbs the development of the fetus and produces a malformation

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — is inherited from the parents: A teratogen acts from outside and is not inherited

C — causes cancer in the exposed person: An agent that causes cancer is a carcinogen

D — affects only the mother and never the fetus: The whole danger of a teratogen lies in its effect on the fetus

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse asks about drugs and alcohol at the very first antenatal visit, because the early weeks of pregnancy, when the organs are being formed, pass before most women come for care
option_1: causes a structural or functional defect in the developing fetus

question: A 70 year old patient who was independent on admission now needs help with bathing and feeding after a week of illness. The nurse should record this change as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. a change in the nursing diagnosis and the care plan, with the reason for it

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A change in the patient's ability to care for himself alters the nursing diagnosis and the plan of care, and the revision is recorded with its reason

🔍 Key Clues: 70 year old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a reason to discharge the patient: Discharge is a medical decision and not a nursing response to increased dependency

B — a complaint against the attendants: The attendants have not been shown to be at fault

D — a note that the patient is lazy: A patient who has lost function is not lazy

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reassesses the patient at every shift and not only on admission, because a care plan that is written once and never revised is a plan that describes a patient who has since changed
option_3: a change in the nursing diagnosis and the care plan, with the reason for it
option_4: a note that the patient is lazy

question: The nurse's record of a patient should always be written in:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. ink, in a clear hand and without any overwriting or blank space

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The record is written in ink, legibly, with no overwriting and with no blank space left, so that no entry can be altered or added later

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — pencil, so that it can be corrected later: A pencil entry can be erased and is not accepted as a permanent record

B — the language that the patient speaks: The clinical record is kept in the language of the institution

C — a shorthand understood only by the nurses of the ward: A record meant for the whole treating team must be readable by all of them

option_4: ink, in a clear hand and without any overwriting or blank space

question: The single most effective measure for preventing infection acquired in hospital is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. hand hygiene at the correct moment with the correct technique

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Hand hygiene before and after contact with a patient remains the single most effective measure against infection acquired in hospital

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — wearing gloves for every task: Gloves protect the wearer and are not a substitute for washing the hands

B — giving prophylactic antibiotics to every patient: Antibiotics given without indication breed resistant organisms

D — isolating every patient in a single room: Single room isolation is not possible for every patient and is not necessary for most

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

option_3: hand hygiene at the correct moment with the correct technique
option_4: isolating every patient in a single room

question: In a 30 year old man who has been rescued from drowning and is not breathing, the first step is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. open the airway, give two rescue breaths and start chest compressions at a rate of about 100 to 120 a minute

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The airway is opened, two rescue breaths are given and compressions are started at once at the recommended rate while help is called

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give five abdominal thrusts: Abdominal thrusts are used for an obstructed airway and not for a drowned patient

C — wait for the ambulance to arrive: Waiting for the ambulance without any resuscitation wastes the minutes that decide survival

D — place him in a sitting position: Sitting a patient who is not breathing obstructs the airway further

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse continues the resuscitation until the patient recovers or the team declares death, because the rule of the drowned patient is that he is not dead until he is warm and dead
option_2: open the airway, give two rescue breaths and start chest compressions at a rate of about 100 to 120 a minute

question: A 35 year old man is brought unconscious after taking an unknown number of sleeping tablets two hours ago. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. keep the airway clear, position him on his side, arrange gastric lavage as ordered and take a sample of the stomach wash to the laboratory

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The airway and the position come first, and the lavage or the activated charcoal is given on order with the first sample of the wash sent for analysis

🔍 Key Clues: 35 year old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give him a strong cup of coffee: Coffee does not counteract a sedative and may cause vomiting and aspiration

B — make him walk about the ward to wake him: Walking an unconscious or drowsy patient invites a fall

D — leave him to sleep it off: A patient who has taken an overdose is a medical emergency and cannot be left

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse sends the empty strip or the bottle with the patient, because the antidote is chosen from the name on the strip and not from the depth of the unconsciousness
option_1: give him a strong cup of coffee
option_2: make him walk about the ward to wake him
option_3: keep the airway clear, position him on his side, arrange gastric lavage as ordered and take a sample of the stomach wash to the laboratory

question: The earliest clinical sign of hypovolaemic shock in an adult is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. a rise in the pulse rate with a narrowing pulse pressure

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A rise in the pulse rate with a narrowing pulse pressure appears before the systolic pressure falls, because the body compensates by constricting the peripheral vessels

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — anuria: Anuria comes when the loss is severe

C — deep and rapid breathing: Rapid deep breathing follows a severe metabolic disturbance

D — a fall in the systolic blood pressure: A fall in the systolic pressure is a later sign in a young adult

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

option_1: a rise in the pulse rate with a narrowing pulse pressure
option_4: a fall in the systolic blood pressure

question: Six hours after an abdominal operation a 50 year old woman has a pulse of 118 a minute, a blood pressure of 96/60 mm Hg and a dressing that is dry on the surface but with a firm swelling beneath it. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. report the findings at once as a concealed haemorrhage under the dressing

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A tachycardia with a falling pressure and a swelling that is firm beneath a dry dressing points to bleeding within the wound and needs immediate reporting

🔍 Key Clues: 50 year old | 60 mm

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — change the dressing and apply pressure: Changing the dressing is done by the surgeon and covers the sign rather than treating it

C — raise the foot of the bed and give a hot drink: Oral fluid is withheld in a patient who may need a return to the theatre

D — record the findings and review in two hours: Two hours of waiting may be two hours of concealed bleeding

option_1: report the findings at once as a concealed haemorrhage under the dressing

option_4: record the findings and review in two hours

question: The position of choice for an unconscious patient without any spinal injury is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. lateral with the face turned to one side

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The lateral position keeps the tongue forward and lets the secretions drain out of the mouth instead of into the airway

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — prone with the face down: A face down position obstructs the airway

option_4: lateral with the face turned to one side

question: A patient on chemotherapy has a white cell count of 1200 per cubic millimetre. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. keep him in a protective environment, restrict visitors with infection and report any fever at once

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A very low white cell count leaves the patient open to infection, so he is protected from contact and any rise of temperature is reported at once

question: A patient with chronic renal failure has a rising potassium level. The nurse should withhold:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. orange juice and bananas

question: A woman at 36 weeks of gestation reports a sudden painless bright red vaginal bleeding. The nurse should:

question: A newborn delivered at term has a respiratory rate of 72 a minute with grunting and nasal flaring an hour after birth. The nurse should:

question: A woman who has completed her family wishes a permanent method of contraception. The method most commonly offered to her in the national programme is:
solution:

question: A mother asks the nurse how much clean water should be added to one packet of oral rehydration salts. The nurse should reply:

question: The method of health education that is most useful for a group of women who cannot read is:

question: The sex ratio of a population is usually expressed as the:

solution:

question: A 3 year old child is brought at night with a barking cough, hoarseness and a harsh noise on breathing in, but is alert and not drooling. The nurse should:

question: The specific antidote used in paracetamol poisoning is:
solution:

question: A patient on a continuous heparin infusion develops bleeding from the gum and the puncture sites. The drug that should be kept ready to reverse the effect is:

question: A 10 month old infant with diarrhoea is lethargic, has sunken eyes and a skin fold that goes back very slowly. The nurse should:
solution:

question: The upper chamber of the human heart is called the:
solution:

question: The valve that lies between the left atrium and the left ventricle is the:

question: A patient with depression has just been started on an antidepressant. The nurse should watch most closely in the first two weeks for:

question: The culture medium commonly used for the isolation of the tubercle bacillus is:

question: Metaplasia is best defined as:
solution:

question: The cheapest and best source of protein in a vegetarian diet is:
solution:

question: The main end product of protein metabolism that is excreted in the urine is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. urea

question: A patient who accuses the nurses of being hostile towards him while he himself is angry with his family is using the defence mechanism of:

question: The total quantity of blood in a healthy adult is about:

question: A hospital has 250 beds, of which 40 per cent are occupied by surgical patients. The number of surgical patients is:

question: The average of 7, 11, 15 and 19 is:

✅ Correct Answer: b. 102.9 degrees Fahrenheit

🧠 Method: Fahrenheit is obtained by multiplying the Celsius reading by nine fifths and adding thirty two, so thirty nine point four gives about one hundred and two point nine

⚡ Fast Approach: Substitute into the standard formula and keep the units consistent.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 100.4 degrees Fahrenheit: 100.4 degrees Fahrenheit is about 38 degrees Celsius

C — 99.5 degrees Fahrenheit: 99.5 degrees Fahrenheit is about 37.5 degrees Celsius

D — 104.0 degrees Fahrenheit: 104 degrees Fahrenheit is about 40 degrees Celsius

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse notes the scale on every temperature chart she writes in, because a reading of 39.4 entered in a chart meant for Fahrenheit looks like a mild fever and is in fact a high one

question: An infant weighs 4 kg and the daily fluid requirement is 150 mL for each kilogram of body weight. The fluid to be given in twenty four hours is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 600 mL

🧠 Method: One hundred and fifty millilitres for each kilogram multiplied by four kilograms gives six hundred millilitres in twenty four hours

⚡ Fast Approach: Substitute into the standard formula and keep the units consistent.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 750 mL: 750 mL would be the requirement of a 5 kg infant

C — 500 mL: 500 mL would be correct for an infant of 3.3 kg

D — 400 mL: 400 mL would be the requirement of a 2.7 kg infant

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse divides the daily volume by the number of feeds before she starts the day, because a volume that is decided afresh at each feed is the way an infant is given either too much or too little fluid

question: If A is 1, B is 2, C is 3 and so on, the value of the word BAD is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 7

🧠 Method: B is 2, A is 1 and D is 4, and the three together give seven

⚡ Fast Approach: Compare the first and last letters of the given pair to find the shift.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 6: 6 would make one of them worth one less

B — 8: 8 would need a letter that is not in the word

D — 5: 5 would make one of the letters worth less than it is

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse writes the number under each letter before adding, because adding the letters in the order they are read is where such a question is usually lost

question: Complete the series: 2, 9, 28, 65, ?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 126

🧠 Method: Each term is one more than a cube, so the terms are one plus one, eight plus one, twenty seven plus one and sixty four plus one, and the next is one hundred and twenty five plus one

⚡ Fast Approach: Check the differences first, then squares, cubes or multiplication.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 124: 124 would be one hundred and twenty three plus one and 123 is not a cube

C — 120: 120 is not one more than a cube

D — 130: 130 is five more than a cube

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse recognises a series by its shape before working on it, because a series that grows steeply is almost always built on squares, cubes or powers

question: Complete the series: 13, 26, 39, 52, ?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 65

🧠 Method: Each term is thirteen more than the term before it, so fifty two plus thirteen gives sixty five

⚡ Fast Approach: Check the differences first, then squares, cubes or multiplication.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 68: 68 is not a multiple of thirteen

B — 62: 62 is not a multiple of thirteen

D — 60: 60 is not a multiple of thirteen

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse reads a series of multiples of a number as a multiplication table, because the table of thirteen is familiar and the answer is then certain and quick

question: P is the brother of Q and Q is the daughter of R. How is P related to R?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. son

🧠 Method: Q is a daughter of R and P is her brother, so P is also a child of R and therefore his son

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw the family tree and mark the given relations before answering.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — nephew: A nephew is the son of one's brother or sister

C — father: R is the parent and P the child, so the relation is the other way round

D — brother: A brother of R would be P's uncle

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse draws each person in his own place on the family tree before answering, because a relation that is read in the reverse direction gives an answer that sounds right and is quite wrong

question: In a queue of 25 children Ravi stands eleventh from the front. His position from the last is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 15th

🧠 Method: The position from the other end is the total plus one minus the given position, so twenty five plus one minus eleven gives fifteen

⚡ Fast Approach: Positions add up to one more than the total number in the row.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 16th: 16th would need 10 from the front

C — 13th: 13th would need a position of 13 from the front

D — 14th: 14th would need 12 from the front

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse adds the one before subtracting, because the child himself is counted in both the positions and is left out by a plain subtraction

question: All nurses are honest. Some honest people are rich. Which of the following follows?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Some honest people are nurses

🧠 Method: Since every nurse is honest, the honest people must include the nurses, so at least some honest people are nurses

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw the circles of the given sets and see which conclusion is certain.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — No nurse is rich: Nothing in the statements rules out a rich nurse

B — Some nurses are rich: The rich honest people may be quite separate from the nurses

C — All honest people are nurses: The first statement does not say that every honest person is a nurse

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse draws the circles before deciding, because a conclusion that is not forced by the picture is a conclusion that has been assumed and not proved

question: If today is Saturday, what day of the week was it 20 days ago?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Sunday

🧠 Method: Twenty days is two weeks and six days, and six days back from Saturday brings the day to Sunday

⚡ Fast Approach: Use the remainder after dividing by 7 for days, and 30 degrees per hour for clocks.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Friday: Friday is one day back

C — Monday: Monday is five days back

D — Tuesday: Tuesday is four days back

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: The nurse divides the number of days by seven and uses the remainder, because the day that is worked out without that step lands on the wrong date and a wrong date in a follow up letter brings the patient on a day when the clinic is closed
